t: You're on Brixton Hill, a road of about a kilometre running between Brixton and Streatham Hill in south London. Quite a few notable people have connections to it. The surgeon Sir William Blizard died here, as did the Nonconformist minister William Morley Punshon and the landscape painter Edmund John Niemann, whose work hangs in Wolverhampton Art Gallery. Edward Coleman, who played cricket for Essex and was killed in the First World War, lived here. Bertie Joyce, an RAF pilot in the Second World War, was born on this road.
